Below is a concise, high‑level roadmap you can follow once you have the dataset in hand. Adjust each step to the specifics of your data (size, type, business goal, etc.): | Phase | Goal | Typical Actions | Tools / Libraries | |-------|------|----------------|-------------------| | **1️⃣ Understand & Audit** | Know what you have | • Load the data and generate a data‑dictionary
• Check row/column counts, data types, missingness, duplicates, outliers
• Visualize distributions (histograms, box‑plots) | pandas, pandas‑profiling, Sweetviz, Jupyter | | **2️⃣ Clean & Preprocess** | Make the data model‑ready | • Impute or drop missing values (mean/median, KNN, model‑based)
• Encode categoricals (one‑hot, target encoding, ordinal)
• Scale/normalize numeric features (StandardScaler, MinMax)
• Remove or treat outliers (IQR, Z‑score, robust models) | scikit‑learn, feature‑engine, pyjanitor | | **3️⃣ Feature Engineering** | Boost signal | • Create domain‑specific features (ratios, time‑differences, text n‑grams, embeddings)
• Perform dimensionality reduction if needed (PCA, t‑SNE, UMAP)
• Conduct feature importance analysis (mutual information, chi‑square) | pandas, sklearn.decomposition, tsfresh, nltk/spacy for text | | **4️⃣ Exploratory Data Analysis (EDA)** | Spot patterns & hypotheses | • Correlation heatmaps, pair‑plots, group‑by summaries
• Visualize target vs. predictors (box‑plots, violin plots, bar charts)
• Check class balance for classification tasks | seaborn, matplotlib, plotly, pandas‑profiling | | **5️⃣ Define Modeling Objective** | Choose the right problem type | • **Regression** → predict a continuous value
• **Classification** → predict categories (binary/multi‑class)
• **Clustering** → discover natural groups
• **Time‑Series Forecasting** → predict future points
• **Anomaly Detection** → flag unusual records | Depends on business goal | | **6️⃣ Model Selection & Baselines** | Establish a performance floor | • Simple baselines: mean/median predictor, logistic regression, decision tree
• More powerful models: Random Forest, Gradient Boosting (XGBoost, LightGBM, CatBoost), Neural Nets (Keras/PyTorch) | scikit‑learn, xgboost, lightgbm, catboost, keras | | **7️⃣ Hyper‑parameter Tuning** | Optimize performance | • GridSearchCV / RandomizedSearchCV
• Bayesian optimization (Optuna, Hyperopt, Scikit‑Optimize) | scikit‑learn, optuna | | **8️⃣ Model Evaluation** | Validate reliably | • Split strategy: train/validation/test or cross‑validation (StratifiedKFold for classification)
• Metrics: RMSE/MAE for regression, Accuracy/F1/AUC for classification, Silhouette for clustering, MAPE for forecasting | scikit‑learn.metrics, mlflow | | **9️⃣ Interpretability & Validation** | Trust & compliance | • Feature importance (SHAP, LIME)
• Partial dependence plots
• Check for data leakage, fairness, and overfitting | shap, lime, eli5 | | **🔟 Deployment / Monitoring** | Put model into production | • Serialize model (pickle, joblib, ONNX)
• Serve via REST API (FastAPI, Flask) or batch pipeline (Airflow, Prefect)
• Set up monitoring for drift, latency, and performance decay | Docker, FastAPI, MLflow, Evidently AI | | **🔁 Iterate** | Continuous improvement | • Collect new data, retrain, and re‑evaluate regularly | CI/CD pipelines, DVC for data versioning | ### Possible “Best Paths” Depending on Typical Scenarios | Business Scenario | Recommended Path | |-------------------|------------------| | **Predictive sales / demand** | Time‑series forecasting → Prophet / ARIMA → Gradient Boosting on engineered lag features | | **Customer churn / risk scoring** | Binary classification → Imbalanced handling (SMOTE, class weights) → XGBoost + SHAP for explainability | | **Segmenting users** | Unsupervised clustering → Dimensionality reduction (PCA/UMAP) → DBSCAN or HDBSCAN → Validate clusters with business KPIs | | **Anomaly detection in logs** | Isolation Forest / One‑Class SVM / Autoencoder → Thresh
